text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a single, high-contrast focus ring that follows tab order—no exceptions. This ensures keyboard users always see where they are, which is critical for people who rely on keyboards or switch devices. The trade-off is visual clutter for mouse users, but that’s minor compared to the accessibility cost of inconsistent or missing focus indicators.

name: Reader
text: The single high-contrast ring fails sighted keyboard users with cognitive load—it’s a flashing neon sign screaming “YOU ARE HERE” every time they tab, breaking flow. Instead, use a subtle, low-contrast ring that only appears after a short delay, proving it’s needed without shouting. Test with real keyboard users: if they complete tasks faster with the delayed ring, it wins.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a single, subtle focus ring that appears only after a 250ms delay and stays until the next tab. This keeps sighted keyboard users from feeling hounded while still giving them clear feedback—no neon sign, just a quiet guide. The trade-off is that users who tab quickly might miss the ring, but that’s rare and far better than constant distraction.

name: Reader
text: The 250ms delay risks missing the ring entirely for users who tab at 125ms intervals—common for power users. A better alternative: keep the high-contrast ring but make it toggleable via a user setting, letting individuals choose between clarity and minimalism. Settle it with real user testing—measure task completion time and error rates with both versions.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Ship a **high-contrast focus ring with a 125ms delay, toggleable via user setting**—tested with real users to balance clarity and minimalism. Owner: Ramp.
